description.value:
Trigger You Mark a creature.

Area 10-foot emanation from the Marked creature

Marking a creature makes nearby lesser creatures briefly off-guard from proximity dread.

Creatures in the area whose level is lower than the Marked creature's are off-guard until the end of your next turn. This is a mental fear effect, and a creature that is immune to fear is unaffected.

cinderfall.incomplete: The Mark itself is now built (waywarden.mark-quarry.json grants TokenMark slug 'quarry'). The "Trigger: You Mark a creature" clause needs no rule-element hook -- like real pf2e's own reactions, the trigger is player-adjudicated text, not something the system enforces. The real, still-unresolved blocker: even with a Mark, there's no roll option comparing an arbitrary set of nearby creatures' levels against a third creature's (the Marked one) level -- no relative-level comparison predicate exists in pf2e-source (pf2e's own numeric-comparison predicates, e.g. {"lte": ["target:hp-percent", 50]}, compare a roll option against a literal number, not two different creatures' levels against each other).
